summary: NASA announced plans to accelerate its Artemis program to return astronauts to the Moon, even as researchers reported that the Artemis II launch created a temporary disruption in Earth's upper atmosphere that affected GPS signals. Meanwhile, NASA's Swift space telescope re-entered Earth's atmosphere following a failed rescue attempt, concluding two decades of cosmic explosion observations and prompting NASA to solicit industry proposals to preserve the Hubble Space Telescope. In commercial developments, Starfish Space cut its SSPICY mission short after losing contact with its Otter vehicle, while Orbital Matter and EnduroSat announced a planned 2028 joint in-space manufacturing mission, and Sceye signed an agreement to fly a high-altitude platform fleet for SoftBank. NASA also selected awardees for Ka-Band satellite relay systems to enhance space communications infrastructure. In planetary science and space exploration, Europe's Hera probe captured its first images of the asteroid Dimorphos, while recent research indicates active volcanism beneath Mars' surface and data from the James Webb Space Telescope revealed candidate seeds for heavy black holes. In military aerospace developments, Shield AI transitioned its X-BAT autonomous drone prototype into testing, as General Atomics and the U.S. Air Force Research Laboratory evaluated next steps for autonomous drone concepts. Skywatchers tonight can watch for peak activity from the Taurid meteor shower, which is expected to feature prominent fireballs.
